name: MADAGASCAR

flag.title: Madagascar
flag.note: White & red vertical, then red over green

lead: Madagascar is the fourth-largest island in the world. It drifted away from Africa 170 million years ago. About 90% of its animals live nowhere else. Scientists call it the eighth continent.
geo: Madagascar lies 400 km off the coast of Africa. Rainforest covers the east. The dry west has giant baobabs and sharp limestone towers called tsingy.
The south is almost desert. Red soil gives Madagascar the nickname Great Red Island. Humpback whales breed in the warm sea each winter.
animals: Over 100 kinds of lemur live here. The mouse lemur weighs just 30 grams, the smallest primate on Earth. The indri's wail echoes for kilometres.
The fossa looks like a small puma but is kin to the mongoose. Half the world's chameleons live here, including the thumbnail-sized Brookesia micra.
culture: Malagasy people honour their ancestors, called razana. In the famadihana, families lift the bones, wrap them in fresh silk and dance with them.
Rice is sacred. People eat it three times a day. The national dish, romazava, is a zebu-beef stew with wild greens. Zebu cattle appear in every ceremony.
history: Sailors from Indonesia crossed 6,000 km of ocean and settled here about 2,000 years ago. Bantu farmers came later. By the 1700s the Merina kingdom ruled much of the island.
France took over in 1896 and ended the monarchy. A fierce uprising in 1947 killed tens of thousands. Madagascar became independent on 26 June 1960.
wows: Madagascar grows about 80% of the world's vanilla, yet is very poor.
The first settlers came from Indonesia, not nearby Africa.
About 59 chameleon species live nowhere else on Earth.
Animals shelter inside tsingy spires, safe from human hunters.
Malagasy is closer to Malay than to Swahili.
No zoo has kept an indri alive for long.
Fady are family taboos: one bans eel, another bans facing north at meals.

myths.myth: Baobab trees only grow in Africa
myths.fact: Six of the world's eight baobab kinds grow in Madagascar. Africa has one.
Lemurs are an older branch of primates. They split off before monkeys appeared.
